concerns.text: FR-003 mandates 1,000 random‑sign permutations *within each window*. Task T008 implements only 500 permutations per selected window and then re‑uses that null for all 300 windows, weakening the functional requirement and violating Constitution VII (exactly 1,000 permutations per window).

FR-003 also requires permutations to be generated for *every* window under test. T008 builds the null distribution from only the first 20 windows per interval length and applies it to the remaining windows, silently narrowing the scope of the requirement without a spec amendment.

SC-001 contains a literal '[deferred]' placeholder for the required fraction of lags whose 95 % CI must contain zero, making the success criterion unmeasurable; downstream task T015 cannot verify compliance because no concrete threshold exists.
SC-003 lists '[deferred]' for the estimated runtime upper bound, leaving only the hard 6‑hour limit testable. This omission prevents verification of the intended performance target.

The schema requires the columns 'sensitivity_flag' and 'theoretical_variance' in the final 'autocorrelation_stats.csv'. No task (T008, T009, T011) writes these columns, so schema validation will fail.

Task T011 reruns the permutation engine (500 permutations) for all 300 windows with four zero‑density variants each, totaling ~600,000 permutations. The plan estimates only ~1 hour runtime, which is inconsistent with the actual computational load and likely exceeds SC-003's 6‑hour limit.

The specification requires handling of all‑zero windows (skip or warn) and reporting p‑values of exactly 0 or 1 as '<0.001' / '>0.999'. No task in the list addresses these edge cases, so the implementation would violate the acceptance criteria.

The 'adjustment' column enum is defined as placeholder values ('+[deferred]', '‑[deferred]'), while task T011 outputs concrete adjustments (e.g., '+5%'). This mismatch means the generated CSV cannot satisfy the contract.

Spec SC-006 requires heatmap resolution ≥ 1000 × 1000 px. Task T012 demands ≥ 1200 × 1200 px, which is stricter but introduces a discrepancy in the documented verification threshold; the verification script must be aligned to a single canonical value.
